items.title: Questions regarding 5HP + 5W2
items.author: AIDream
items.text:
Dear all， I am currently implementing a scenario combining 5HP and 5W2 My Scenario: 
 Entity 1010 sells raw material RM12 to Entity 1710 . 
 Entity 1710 uses RM12 to produce finished good FG126 . 
 Entity 1710 then sells FG126 back to Entity 1010 . I have four specific questions regarding this setup: 1. Valuation Class Compatibility 
 Could you confirm if the system supports the following mixed valuation setup within this integrated flow? 
 RM12: Valuated as Standard Price (S) in 1010, but as Moving Average Price (V) in 1710. 
 FG126: Valuated as Standard Price (S) in 1710, but as Moving Average Price (V) in 1010. 
 Does the standard 5W2 logic handle these cross-plant valuation differences correctly without issues? 2. Return Process Restrictions (Note 3192546) 
 Regarding SAP Note 3192546 , it states: "Customer return processes with reference to the advanced intercompany stock transfer process are not supported. Please use an intercompany stock transfer return." 
 Could you clarify the practical implication of this? Does this mean that to process a return, I must manually create a new STO with reversed quantity and direction (from buyer back to seller), rather than referencing the original inbound delivery or sales order directly? 3. Group Valuation with Multiple Suppliers 
 In a scenario where multiple production plants supply the same finished good to a single receiving plant—for example, both Plant 1710 and Plant 1310 produce FG126 and sell it to Plant 1010 —how does the system determine the Group Valuation Price at the receiving plant (1010)? 
 Since the production costs (and thus the intercompany transfer prices) might differ between 1710 and 1310, what is the logic used to update or maintain the Group Valuation Price for FG126 in Plant 1010? Is it based on the latest goods receipt, or a weighted average? 4. Purchasing View Extension for Finished Goods 
 In our business scenario, Plant 1010 needs to purchase FG126 from both Plant 1710 and Plant 1210. However, since FG126 is set up as a Finished Product , the system does not natively display the Purchasing view . 
 What is the standard SAP procedure to handle this requirement? Is it permissible (or recommended) to extend the Purchasing view specifically for Plant 1010 so it can procure this material via Intercompany STO , or is there an alternative configuration workaround (such as a separate material type) to achieve this flow? Thank you for your guidance. Best regards,

items.title: How to create regular OR-type sales orders with reference to sales scheduling agreements?
items.author: xuqi_fangaf39f1
items.text:
Dear SAP Support Team, 
 In SAP Public Cloud, the system does not allow creating new copy control entries for sales documents. 
 Our business requirement is as follows: 
 We release sales forecasts via scheduling agreements. After the formal customer order is confirmed, we need to create standard OR sales orders with reference to the scheduling agreement to offset the previously posted sales forecast. 
 Currently, the system prevents us from creating OR orders referencing scheduling agreements due to the restriction on copy control configuration. 
 Business logic details: 
 We use scheduling agreements to capture long-term customer sales forecasts, which drive supply planning and material availability. These forecast quantities are not binding customer orders. 
 When the customer confirms the firm order, we need to generate a standard OR sales order against the existing scheduling agreement. The purpose of this OR order is to consume / offset the previously forecasted quantity from the scheduling agreement, so that the forecast is replaced by firm order demand. 
 Without this reference creation, demand figures will be duplicated in our supply planning: both the forecast from scheduling agreement and the new standalone OR order will be active, leading to over-planning and incorrect material commitment. 
 Could you please advise what alternative approaches are available to support this business scenario? Does SAP provide a standard solution for this requirement?

deep_dives.explanation:
The post describes embedded AI in ABAP Cloud that relies on SAP AI Core and the Generative AI Hub. The connection is set up through a BTP service instance and key, a communication arrangement for scenario `SAP_COM_0A69`, and an intelligent scenario managed in ISLM. These steps come before any ABAP code and are the likely cause of failures.

The ABAP side is small. You get the factory with `cl_aic_islm_compl_api_factory=>get( )`, call `create_instance( 'Z_MY_SCENARIO' )` with your ISLM scenario ID, then call `execute_for_string( )` with the prompt and read the result with `get_completion( )`. The SDK also has a Prompt Library API and exception handling, so wrap the call in a TRY block and catch the SDK's exceptions.

Orchestration adds data masking and document grounding, but the excerpt stops before details. Availability is listed for S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and On-Premise, Public Edition, and the SAP Business AI Platform ABAP environment. Confirm class and method names against the current ABAP cheat sheet before teaching, since only the excerpt was available.

deep_dives.title: Range copy vs FOR projection: what ends up in the table
deep_dives.explanation:
A select-option `s_bukrs` is a range table with `sign`, `option`, `low`, `high`. If the target `gt_bukrs` has the same range line type, `gt_bukrs = s_bukrs.` copies every row with all four components. That is the shortest and correct way to duplicate a range.

A `VALUE #( FOR ls IN s_bukrs ( ls-low ) )` expression builds a table whose line type is whatever the target has. For a plain table of `bukrs` it keeps only `low` and drops sign and option. So an exclude row or a pattern option would silently become a plain value. The two forms are therefore not interchangeable; the choice depends on the target type.

Projection becomes useful when you need to filter or transform, for example `FOR ls IN s_bukrs WHERE ( sign = 'I' AND option = 'EQ' ) ( ls-low )`. The thread's snippets also had errors: looping over a field symbol that was never assigned a table does not compile. Remember that `LOOP AT ... INTO DATA(...)` needs 7.40 SP08 or later.

deep_dives.title: PDF output from a RAP business object
deep_dives.explanation:
The post lays out a chain for S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise. A Form Data Provider CDS view supplies the data. An Adobe Form designed in ADT is bound to the fields through XML. A RAP action triggers PDF generation, and a Fiori extension on the Object Page downloads the result. No code is in the excerpt, so the layer boundaries are what you can take from it.

Failure points are at each layer: the CDS data provider must return the structure the form expects, the XML binding names must match, the RAP action must return the PDF in a form the UI can consume, and the Object Page extension must call the action and handle the binary result. The author reports it took days, which suggests the wiring is not obvious.

For teaching, build the layers one at a time and test each in isolation, rather than debugging the whole chain at once.

post_drafts.title: Range copy vs FOR
post_drafts.text:
*Quick ABAP check:* are these the same?

`gt_bukrs = s_bukrs.`
`gt_bukrs = VALUE #( FOR ls IN s_bukrs ( ls-low ) ).`

No.

The first copies *sign, option, low, high* (if types match).
The second keeps only *LOW* and drops sign/option, so an exclude row becomes a plain value.

Use FOR when you filter or project, e.g. `WHERE ( sign = 'I' )`.

interview_questions.question: A colleague replaces gt_bukrs = s_bukrs with a VALUE #( FOR ... ( ls-low ) ) expression. What changes?
interview_questions.answer: The direct assignment copies every row of the range table including sign, option, low and high, provided the target has the same line type. The FOR expression with ( ls-low ) builds rows from the LOW component only. If the target is a plain table of BUKRS, sign and option are lost, so exclusions and patterns become simple values. That can change selection results silently. FOR is the right tool when you need to filter, for example WHERE ( sign = 'I' ), or to project a component. For a plain duplicate of a range, use the direct assignment.

interview_questions.question: What must be in place before an ABAP Cloud class can call an LLM through the ABAP AI SDK?
interview_questions.answer: The system needs a connection to SAP AI Core and the Generative AI Hub. That means a BTP service instance and key, a communication arrangement for scenario SAP_COM_0A69, and an intelligent scenario defined in ISLM. In code you get the factory with cl_aic_islm_compl_api_factory=>get( ), create an instance with the scenario ID, call execute_for_string and read the result with get_completion. You should wrap the call in exception handling from the SDK. Orchestration adds data masking and document grounding. Verify the names against current documentation.

interview_questions.question: How would you design access control so an AI agent calling SAP data via MCP respects the end user's authorizations?
interview_questions.answer: Do not use a shared technical user. Propagate the real user identity end to end, for example through OAuth 2.0 and X.509 certificates with Cloud Connector, as in the PoC. The backend must authorize each call, so a user without permission gets no data. In the PoC, the agent saw none of the four orders. Additionally, keep credentials in BTP destinations and put an API gateway such as SAP API Management in front to apply policies. Test the negative case first, since it proves enforcement lies in the backend and not in the agent.
